chunks: With this chain of transmission, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah, who said:

I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a menstruating woman making up the salat (prayer), and then making up the fasting. He said: “She is not required to make up the salat (prayer), but she must make up the sawm (fasting) of the month of Ramadan.”

Then he turned toward me and said: “Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to command Fāṭimah عليها السلام regarding that, and she would command the believing women regarding that.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: When she wishes to attain taharah (ritual purity) by ghusl (ritual bath), she must first examine herself with a piece of cotton that she inserts, then removes. If blood comes out on it, then she is still menstruating, so she should leave the ghusl (ritual bath) until she becomes pure. But if it comes out clean of blood, then she should wash her private part, then perform wudu (ablution) as for salat (prayer), beginning with rinsing the mouth and drawing water into the nose, then washing her face and her hands, and wiping her head and the upper parts of her feet. Then she performs ghusl (ritual bath), beginning with washing her head, then her right side, then her left side. If she leaves the rinsing of the mouth and drawing water into the nose in her wudu (ablution), there is no hardship upon her in that.

key_terms.الِاسْتِنْشَاقَ: drawing water into the nose as part of washing
key_terms.صَوْمَ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the obligatory fasting of the month of Ramadan
key_terms.قَضَاءِ: making up an act of worship after its time has passed

ai.seo_question: Does a menstruating woman make up missed prayers and fasting in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that a menstruating woman does not make up missed salat (prayer) but must make up the missed sawm (fasting) of Ramadan. It also transmits that this ruling was instructed by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم to Fāṭimah عليها السلام, and includes a legal explanation of how a woman verifies the end of menstruation and performs purification through wudu (ablution) and ghusl (ritual bath).
